ORD-01.title: Double submit at checkout places two Orders from one Cart (no idempotency)
ORD-01.fixed_by: c800e71 (7.1): placeOrder calls lockCart(input.owner, tx) (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on carts) before getCart at src/modules/ordering/internal/place.ts:192; lockCart at src/modules/cart/internal/cart.ts:193; clearCart runs in the same transaction (place.ts:306). Test tests/db/place-order.test.ts:267 'places one Order when the same Cart is submitted twice at once' asserts one Order, one cart_problem and pickup_window_usage drinks 2.
ORD-01.problem: Fixed in 7.1: the second placement on the same Cart waits on the Cart row lock and then finds the Cart empty.
ORD-01.reasoning: Default Prisma isolation on Postgres is READ COMMITTED (no isolationLevel set anywhere in src), so after the lock wait getCart takes a new snapshot and sees the lines the first transaction deleted. The second call returns cart_problem, so no second Order, Order Code or Capacity is taken. The db test runs two placeOrder calls at once against the real test database.
ORD-01.corrections: The audit's preferred nonce-and-redirect was not built. The second request gets 'Something in your Cart changed. Check your Cart.' (checkout/actions.ts:44) instead of the existing Order, so after a pre-hydration double tap, where the browser keeps the second response, the Customer can land on that message with an empty Cart while their one Order exists. That is a small UX follow-up (low), not the duplicate-Order bug.

ORD-02.title: Signing in with a Guest Cart crashes the first page (concurrent mergeGuestCart: P2002 / P2025)
ORD-02.fixed_by: c800e71 (7.1): currentCartOwner wrapped in React cache() (src/modules/cart/internal/session.ts:24); mergeGuestCart locks the Guest Cart first and returns if it is gone (src/modules/cart/internal/cart.ts:214). Test tests/db/cart.test.ts:151 runs two merges at once.
ORD-02.problem: The hk_cart cookie is still never cleared after a merge, so every page a signed-in Member opens (the header CartButton calls currentCartOwner) still opens a merge transaction (BEGIN, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, COMMIT) for up to 30 days. The crash is gone, but this part of the finding's impact remains as wasted database round trips.
ORD-02.fix: Check for a Guest Cart with a plain findUnique on the token hash before opening the merge transaction, so the common case costs one read. Or run the merge once from a Server Action or the sign-in callback that also deletes the hk_cart cookie.
ORD-02.reasoning: The P2002/P2025 race is closed: the second merge blocks on the Guest Cart row lock and, once the first commits and deletes the row, the SELECT FOR UPDATE returns no rows and it returns early; cache() also dedupes the header and page call within one request. grep shows hk_cart is only read or set (session.ts:25, 41, 44), never deleted, so the per-request transaction described in the impact still happens.
ORD-02.corrections: Main problem (error page on first render after sign-in) is fixed; only the leftover per-request merge transaction remains.

ORD-03.title: Late paid webhook after Expire/Cancel is silently ignored: Customer charged, no Order, no log, no in-app refund
ORD-03.fixed_by: b59c16f (7.2): recordPaymentEvent locks the Payment row and accepts a paid event unless already paid or refunded (src/modules/payments/internal/payments.ts:96-118); a refused transition(paid) becomes paid_late and is refunded after the commit (src/modules/ordering/internal/webhook.ts:52-64); closeCheckout calls expireCheckout first and keeps the Payment open if the provider refuses (payments.ts:131-144). Test tests/db/payments.test.ts:187 'refunds a payment that lands after the Order expired'.
ORD-03.problem: If the automatic late refund fails at the provider, refundPayment puts the Payment back to paid, the webhook only logs 'refund by hand' and answers 200 (so the provider never retries), and refundOrder still refuses Expired Orders and unpaid-then-Cancelled Orders (paidAt is null), so no Manager can refund it in the app. Meanwhile the Order page tells the Customer 'The refund is on its way.'
ORD-03.fix: Let refundOrder accept a closed Order whose Payment is paid (status expired or cancelled with payment.status paid) and show those Orders on /manage/orders with the Refund button. Add a db test where the provider refund throws for a late payment.
ORD-03.reasoning: The common path is fixed and tested: a late paid event stores providerPaymentId, the Order stays Expired, and a Refund row with actor 'webhook' is written. The fallback branch (webhook.ts:65-70) is the only place the old 'no record, no in-app refund' outcome survives, and it needs both a late payment and a failed provider refund. Test Mode only (ADR 0006), so low.
ORD-03.corrections: No test covers closeCheckout keeping the Payment pending when expireCheckout throws, or the refund-failure branch.

PAY-01.title: Paid webhooks for a Payment that is no longer pending are silently dropped: Customer charged, Order stays Expired/Cancelled/Placed, no refund path
PAY-01.fixed_by: b59c16f (7.2): paid events are accepted for pending, failed and expired Payments under a row lock (src/modules/payments/internal/payments.ts:96-118); a retry after a failed attempt pays the Order (tests/db/payments.test.ts:203); a payment after Expire or Cancel is refunded automatically (webhook.ts:52-64, test payments.test.ts:187); closeCheckout marks expired only after the provider confirms (payments.ts:131-144).
PAY-01.problem: When the automatic refund of a late payment fails at the provider, the Payment stays paid on an Expired or Cancelled Order, the only trace is a console.error, the webhook answers 200 so nothing retries, and refundOrder refuses those Orders, so there is still no in-app refund path for that case. The Customer is told the refund is on its way.
PAY-01.fix: Make refundOrder accept a closed Order whose Payment is paid and list such Orders with a Refund button on /manage/orders (or retry the refund from the daily cron). Cover the provider-refund failure with a db test.
PAY-01.reasoning: Every reproduction in the finding now works: the failed-then-paid case pays the Order (test line 203), the after-expiry case refunds (test line 187), and closeCheckout no longer pre-marks expired. The residual is the same narrow refund-failure fallback as ORD-03.
PAY-01.corrections: A Payment is still marked failed on one failed event, as the audit advised against, but a later paid event is now accepted from failed, so the harm is gone.

PAY-02.title: Payment rows are updated read-then-write with no status guard: closeCheckout can overwrite paid with expired, and concurrent paid events clobber providerPaymentId
PAY-02.fixed_by: b59c16f (7.2): recordPaymentEvent reads the Payment with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (src/modules/payments/internal/payments.ts:96-100) and ignores a paid event once paid or refunded (line 110); closeCheckout's write is updateMany guarded on status pending or failed (payments.ts:141-144). Test tests/db/payments.test.ts:215 'keeps the first payment when two paid events arrive for one checkout'.
PAY-02.problem: Fixed in 7.2: Payment writes are serialized by a row lock and guarded on status.
PAY-02.reasoning: Under READ COMMITTED, closeCheckout's guarded updateMany re-checks status after waiting on the webhook's lock, so it cannot overwrite paid. The second paid event finds status paid and returns ignored, so providerPaymentId keeps the first id and no false 'paid after the Order closed' log is printed. refundPayment's claim is also a guarded updateMany.

PAY-04.title: Refunds are not atomic with the Order transition, and the claim is reverted on errors whose outcome is unknown; both can leave Orders stuck
PAY-04.problem: refundOrder refunds the Payment (refundPayment) and then moves the Order to Refunded in a separate step, so a crash or timeout between the two leaves the Payment refunded and the Order still Picked Up or Cancelled. Every retry then gets already_refunded and answers not_allowed, so the Order never reaches Refunded and the Stars of a Picked Up Order are never taken back.
PAY-04.fix: In refundOrder, when refundPayment answers already_refunded and the Payment has a Refund row, go on to transition(refunded) and the email instead of refusing, so a retry finishes a half-done refund. Leave provider-side reconciliation (keeping the claim on unknown outcomes, refund webhooks) until a PayMongo account exists (ADR 0003).
PAY-04.reasoning: Code is unchanged since the audit (7.2 touched recordPaymentEvent and closeCheckout, not refundPayment or refundOrder). Confirmed: refundPayment claims paid to refunded, calls the provider, writes the Refund row, and reverts to paid on any throw (payments.ts:161-190); refundOrder then calls transition separately and maps already_refunded to not_allowed (refund.ts:43-47). The Manager list keeps showing 'Refund' for such an Order (reads.ts:198-200), and every tap answers 'can't be refunded now'. A process killed mid-call (fetch has no timeout, so a hung provider call ends at the function limit) also leaves the claim without a Refund row. Counter-evidence: the demo runs only on the fake provider (ADR 0003 update: PayMongo paused sign-ups, batch 3.4 skipped), whose refund() never throws, and transition(refunded) cannot be refused after the eligibility check because picked_up and paid cancelled Orders have no other exit and a second refundOrder already stops at the claim. So the stuck state needs a crash in a window of milliseconds. The PayMongo-only parts (refund webhooks mapped to 'other', a timeout after the provider refunded) are latent in an adapter that has never run against a sandbox. The 'no_online_payment for a non-paid Payment' path is unreachable today: a Payment leaves paid only through the refund claim, failed events only touch pending Payments, and closeCheckout only touches pending or failed ones.
PAY-04.corrections: Severity medium to low: no failure path can fire with the fake provider, and no real money moves (ADR 0006). The non-paid Payment case is unreachable, not just latent. The unique index on refunds.payment_id is defensive only: the paid-to-refunded claim already prevents a second Refund row. Effort for the recommended part is S; the auditor's full fix (reconcile through PayMongo refund webhooks) is M and cannot be tested without an account.

ID1-01.title: Account deletion leaves pending sign-in links working; they sign in to a new account with the deleted email
ID1-01.problem: forgetMember deletes verifications where identifier equals the email, but Better Auth 1.7.18 stores sign-in links as identifier 'magic-link:<token>' with the email inside value, so the delete matches nothing. A link sent in the 5 minutes before deletion still works and creates a fresh, empty account with that email, contrary to the docstring.

Better Auth also purges expired verifications on every link check (internal-adapter.mjs:802-806), so the email does not stay in verifications for long. What remains is a dead line, a false docstring and a few minutes of retained email, so it is a correctness and privacy-promise bug of low impact. The rate_limits 'link:<email>' retention is ops:9's housekeeping finding.
ID1-01.corrections: Severity medium to low: 'signed straight back in' is a fresh empty account for the inbox owner within 5 minutes, and the email leaves verifications on the next link check after expiry, not indefinitely. The rate_limits part belongs to ops:9. Same problem as ID2-03, which the audit itself rated low.

ID1-02.problem: The email-link limit is keyed on the address alone (3 per 15 minutes) and is checked before the per-IP limit, so anyone who sends 3 requests per window keeps that person from getting a sign-in link. Better Auth's own magic-link route is in disabledPaths, so this action is the only way to get a link. christian@hoshikopi.example is in prisma/seed-data.ts in the public repo, and on the live demo the seeded accounts sign in through the logs (docs/06-SETUP.md section 9), not Google, so the lockout works there. Members have Google sign-in (live since 2026-11-07) as a way around a lockout, and Staff sessions slide for 7 days, so an already signed-in Manager is not affected. The remaining harm is a targeted nuisance against a portfolio demo. Any per-address cap can be exhausted by someone else, so the fix only raises the cost.

The suggested fix (email+IP plus a looser per-email cap) does not remove a determined lockout, only makes it costlier. Every Manager-level call passes a /manage path today, but a future one that passes '/bar' would skip the Second Factor with nothing to catch it.

The fix should key on the required role argument, not the user's role, or a Manager opening /bar (requireStaff('barista', '/bar')) would be sent to the Second Factor. Related but different: staff:1 is the Bar Screen showing Manager controls that then redirect; tests:13 is the missing access-matrix test.

ID2-02.title: Second Factor pass never expires inside a 7-day sliding session, including on the shared bar tablet
ID2-02.problem: secondFactorPassed only checks that sessions.second_factor_at is set, and Better Auth sessions last 7 days and renew daily with use, so a session that entered the code once keeps full Manager access for as long as it is used. If a Manager enters the code on the shared bar tablet, that tablet stays a full Manager session.

ADR 0014 records 'sessions.second_factor_at marks the session that entered a code', so 'once per session' is the recorded design, and changing it needs an ADR amendment. Counter-evidence on impact: ADR 0005 has the bar tablet signed in as a Barista, and a Barista session never shows Manager controls, so the tablet becomes a Manager session only if a Manager signs in there with their own email link and then enters a code; that is a chain of choices the current UI invites (staff:1) but does not force. On a Manager's own device, a 'remembered' second factor for a sliding week is a common trade-off, and 8.5's 'Sign out everywhere' ends such sessions. For a concept cafe with seeded Staff this is low; a 12-hour age check is a one-line change.
ID2-02.corrections: Severity medium to low: exposure needs a Manager to sign in and enter the code on the shared tablet, and Staff sessions can now be ended from /manage/staff (8.5). The 'no maximum age' part is the same as one of the three points in ID1-13. staff:1 is related (it is why a Manager would enter the code on the tablet) but describes the lost action, not the pass lifetime.

DATA-04.title: No database backstop for Star integrity: duplicate earn, reserve or release per Order and repeat Birthday Treats are all accepted
DATA-04.problem: star_entries has only a sign CHECK and plain indexes, so the database would accept a second earn, reserve, release or reverse row for one Order and a second Birthday Treat in a year. Today only the code keeps each of these to once.
DATA-04.fix: Add a migration with a partial unique index on (order_id, kind) for earn, reserve, release and reverse, and one on (member_id, reason) for birthday rows. Map P2002 to a no-op in the callers and add a db test that a second insert is refused.
DATA-04.reasoning: \d star_entries on the dev database shows the primary key, non-unique member_id and order_id indexes and star_entries_sign_check only; no migration after birthday_sign_check touches the table. The code paths are sound today: earn, release and reverse run inside transition() after SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the Order, and each status is entered once (status.ts:137-176); reserve runs once in placeOrder's transaction; releaseRedemption and reverseForOrder work from net sums; birthdayTreat locks the Member and checks this year first. earnForOrder and reserveRedemption insert with no existence check, so a future caller outside transition() would double-count without the database noticing. It is defence in depth for an integrity rule (ADR 0008), cheap to add, with no current bug.
DATA-04.corrections: 'A retry after a partial failure' cannot double-insert: every Star write sits in the same transaction as its status change, so a failure rolls both back. The risk is a future caller, not a current path. Severity medium to low.
